## DISCOVERY — F001 (NEW)

**FINDING_ID:** F001
**SEVERITY:** 0.68
**FLAW_CLASS:** 5 (correctness — silently-wrong pipeline output)
**ABSTRACTION_INDEX:** 0.45

**FIND:**
`_ALT_HEADER_RE` (`bench/dm/_divergence.py:104–122`) only recognises a dimension tag when it is introduced by the literal keyword `dim`/`dimension`/`on` (`(dim: mechanism)`, `— on: scope`). A **bare parenthesised or dashed dimension** — `Alternative (mechanism)`, `Conjecture (scope)` — is not matched by the `(?P<tag>…)` group, and because the header line is anchored to `$`, the trailing `(mechanism)` token is left unconsumed and **the entire header fails to match**. `parse_alternative_block` then returns `[]`.

This is the exact syntax the module's own docstring uses to name the dimensions: *"differing on a named dimension (mechanism / assumption / scope / timescale / tradeoff)"* (`:13`). A model that mirrors that phrasing is fully §18-compliant yet parses as having supplied *no* alternative.

Empirical evidence (tools ran, output above):
```
bare_parens_no_colon   parsed=0   ← Alternative (mechanism)
keyword_dim_tag        parsed=1   ← Alternative (dim: mechanism)   [control]
```
End-to-end, a fully-compliant finding with a bare-parens header → `compliant=False`, `eta_int_modulator=0.70`.

**FOLLOW:**
`build_divergence_record` → `record.compliant=False` (no admissible alternative, no null block) → `eta_int_modulator` returns **0.70 (hard "ignored the directive" tier)**. That scalar multiplies η_int → `q = η_combined·d·p` → the R_k recurrence `R_k(i)=R_k(i-1)(1−q)/(1−q·R_k(i-1))`. A spurious 0.70 factor **shrinks q, inflating residual risk R_k** for a finding that actually complied. Because the modulator is the *only* consumer of this parse, the corruption is silent — no exception, no failure_reason a human would read as "parser missed a valid header". It biases the whole divergence channel against the most natural compliant syntax, systematically depressing measured convergence. It also crosses into the calibration surface: Exp 39/40 baselines built on this parser will mis-attribute non-compliance.

**ANALYSE:**
Constraint class: **HARD** (correctness — produces a numerically wrong η_int → R_k under valid input; ambiguity defaulted to HARD, and confirmed HARD since a wrong R_k propagates to the calibrated metric).
Premises: (1) §18 accepts a dimension named in parentheses — the docstring itself uses that form; (2) the regex tag grammar requires a `dim:`/`on:` keyword prefix; (3) a header with an unconsumed trailing token cannot satisfy the `$` anchor. Derivation: (1)∧(2)∧(3) ⇒ compliant bare-parens headers are unparsed ⇒ mis-scored 0.70. Concrete: input `"Alternative (mechanism)\ncontrast with primary: …\nlazy strategy …"` → `parsed=0`, `eta=0.70`; the control `"Alternative (dim: mechanism)"` → `parsed=1`. **CONFIRMED.**

Distinctness from C0021: C0021 requires a **trailing colon** after a dim tag (`Alternative 1 (dimension: X):`). My case fails **without any trailing colon** (`Alternative (mechanism)` alone), and the root cause is the *absence of a keyword inside the parens*, not a trailing separator. The proposed fix (below) leaves the trailing-colon case still failing — proving the two are orthogonal defect surfaces.

**FIX:**
Add a third, lowest-priority alternation branch accepting a bare parenthesised/bracketed dimension token, and read it in the parser. `_normalise_dimension` already filters non-dimension tokens, so a stray single-word parenthetical degrades to `dimension=None` (validation-flagged) rather than a silent miss. The keyword branches are listed first, so `(dim: mechanism)` still resolves via `dim_inline`. Multi-word parentheticals (`(see appendix)`) do not match (space before `)` breaks the token), so no false-positive headers.

<<<< SEARCH bench/dm/_divergence.py
    (?P<tag>
        [\(\[]\s*(?:dim(?:ension)?|on)\s*[:=]\s*(?P<dim_inline>[a-zA-Z_-]+)\s*[\)\]]
        |
        [-—]\s*(?:dim(?:ension)?|on)\s*[:=]\s*(?P<dim_dash>[a-zA-Z_-]+)
    )?
====
    (?P<tag>
        [\(\[]\s*(?:dim(?:ension)?|on)\s*[:=]\s*(?P<dim_inline>[a-zA-Z_-]+)\s*[\)\]]
        |
        [-—]\s*(?:dim(?:ension)?|on)\s*[:=]\s*(?P<dim_dash>[a-zA-Z_-]+)
        |
        [\(\[]\s*(?P<dim_bare>[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z_-]*)\s*[\)\]]
    )?
>>>> REPLACE

<<<< SEARCH bench/dm/_divergence.py
        dim_raw = m.group("dim_inline") or m.group("dim_dash")
====
        dim_raw = m.group("dim_inline") or m.group("dim_dash") or m.group("dim_bare")
>>>> REPLACE

**FALSIFICATION:**
FALSIFIER:

Breaking the FIX: applied both SEARCH/REPLACE edits to the real file → 75/75 tests pass, ruff clean, mypy clean; the bare-parens case now yields `compliant=True, eta=1.0`; the C0021 trailing-colon case still fails (untouched); `(see appendix)` still does not match (no false headers). ## VERDICT — CONFIRM C0013

`eta_int_modulator` severe tier 2 (`:835–840`) over-penalises. Verified: a **single** alternative with Jaccard `0.909` — cosmetic (≥0.85) but well below `near_copy_threshold` (0.98) — returns `eta=0.60`, the tier the docstring reserves for "near-copy or recidivism". `all_isomorphic` collapses "one sub-near-copy cosmetic alt" into the severe bucket. Empirically: `iso=0.909, compliant=False, eta=0.60`. Finding and its fix direction are correct. **CONFIRM C0013.**
